verdicts.originalText: While in Nightsoul's Blessing, Chasca's normals collapse to a single Multitarget Fire (Tap) shot per N press (NormalHitNum=1) — the planner renders the Tap frames for any N token. Multitarget Fire (Hold), the multi-bullet element-converted CA used during NS, is not modelled: the schema lacks a primitive for team-element-resolved bullets and for variable-bullet-count CAs. Document the dominant rotation in caveats and accept the fidelity loss for the Hold-CA path.
verdicts.proposedText: Not modeled: the Hold charged-attack mode during Nightsoul's Blessing, which fires up to 6 bullets — some converting to your party's Pyro, Hydro, Cryo, or Electro elements. The timeline shows only the single Tap shot.
verdicts.rationale: The real, decision-relevant point is the omission of the Hold Multitarget Fire — the multi-bullet, party-element-converted charged attack used during the Nightsoul stance (out-of-scope multi-element absorption, CANNOT list). The original buried that under banned spelling 'modelled', banned 'schema', the 'the planner renders' framing, a camelCase internal id 'NormalHitNum=1', a working-behavior sentence (each N press correctly resolves to one Tap shot), and a curator directive. Rewrite keeps the omission plus a short 'timeline shows only Tap' context so the sparse timeline makes sense; every retained claim traces to the caveat and the ability description (up to 6 bullets, PHEC party-based conversion).
